reaction: The explanation makes the lining’s purpose clearer.
reason: The goal calls for connecting lung exchange surfaces to circulating blood, so adding capillaries is a direct next step.
expectation: The capillary sheet will wrap around the air sacs, bringing blood close to air for exchange.

reaction: The close wrapping makes the exchange connection clear, though pressure gradient is not explained here.
reason: Add elastic support to the exchange surface; it appears to be the next part of the sac construction.
expectation: The elastic fibres will support the sacs and perhaps help them recoil during breathing.

effect: The exchange surface now has elastic support, but the result does not explain whether the fibres help it recoil.
reaction: The placement is clear, though I was curious about the fibres’ role in breathing.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the airways toward the sacs.

effect: The airway tree now reaches toward the sacs, ready to join the exchange surface.
reaction: The route is clear, though the result adds little explanation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the airways to the supported sacs.

effect: The airways and supported exchange surfaces now form lungs; the circulation still needs connecting.
reaction: The cutaway brings the pieces together clearly.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the goal of connecting the lungs to circulating blood.
expectation: The lungs will connect to the pulmonary route in the blood-filled circulation, bringing blood to the air-sac capillaries.

effect: The lungs are now connected to circulation, completing the goal. The result also makes clear that continued exchange depends on fresh air reaching the sacs.
reaction: The final connection is clear, though it leaves me curious about how fresh air is moved in and out.

mostWorthwhile.text: Wrapping capillaries around the sacs was the most worthwhile construction: the planned picture connects the thin exchange surface to diffusion of both gases.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding elastic support was less informative: its placement was clear, but the result did not explain its role in breathing.

surprise.text: Surfactant helping prevent the sacs from collapsing as they get smaller clarified why the lining mattered.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though elastic support would have been more meaningful with an explanation of what it does. The pressure gradients driving gas diffusion were also not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, particularly to see how fresh air reaches the sacs, since the ending identifies that as necessary for continued exchange.
